newsitem.title: USA: Bill Cosby pays tribute to son.
newsitem.headline: Bill Cosby pays tribute to son.

text.p: Bill Cosby returned on Monday to work on his TV show for the first time since his son was murdered on a Los Angeles freeway 11 days ago, saying 27-year-old Ennis Cosby would have wanted it that way.

In an interview with CBS News anchorman Dan Rather, Cosby said he could hear his son's spirit saying, "Hey Dad, you have to go back to work. You know, not (because) people want to laugh. Dad you have to go back to work."
In a portion of the interview shown on Monday night on the CBS Evening News, Cosby also denied a claim by a 22-year-old woman, Autumn Jackson, that he was her father.

Jackson and Jose Medina, 51, were arrested nine days ago on charges they demanded money from Cosby to keep them from selling a story to a tabloid newspaper alleging that Jackson was the entertainer's illegitimate daughter.
Cosby admitted to having "a rendezvous' with the girl's mother, but denied being her father.

In a portion of the interview that was not shown on air on Monday night but which was released in a transcript by CBS, Rather asked a follow-up question: "Any possibility that you are the father of this child?"
Cosby answered, "There is a possibility. If you said 'Did you make love to the woman,' the answer is yes. 'Are you the father?' No."

Jackson was released from prison on Monday night after two people guaranteed her $250,000 bond. Jackson, wearing a light blue sweater and black slacks, left the Manhattan federal courthouse holding the arm of her lawyer Robert Baum.
Asked how she felt after being released from federal prison where she has been held for more than a week, she answered softly, "it's nice."

Baum told reporters that Jackson would be returning to California on Monday night to stay with her grandmother, with whom she must stay under conditions of her bail. "It's been very tough for her ... she's happy to be reunited with her family," he said.
Jackson was released after two co-signers, Lois Mayfield and Richard Jesperson, agreed to pay the $250,000 bond if she should flee. Jackson did not have to post any of the money.
Neither Baum nor prosecutors would given any details about the co-signers except that they live in northern California.
Asked about the CBS interview with Cosby, Baum said, "That's a substantial change from the initial comments put forth by Cosby's representatives. His statements are more in line with our defence."
Baum would not, however, give details of that strategy.

Ennis Cosby, 27, was shot in the head as he changed a tire on a Los Angeles freeway early on the morning of Jan. 16. A woman who saw part of the attack gave police a description of the killer as a white male wearing a knit cap, and that was used to put together a composite drawing of the suspect.

Cosby, in his CBS interview, said that his wife Camille was concerned that the killer was still free. "There's a difference in this house," Cosby said. "Mrs. Cosby wants this man. I mean she verbalizes she wants him. She wants him now."
"She refuses to accept the fact that this 'thing' is still out there," Cosby continued. "She doesn't accept the fact that nobody comes forward to help with the truth."
